verdict.rationale: Qdrant documents both modes the story asks for: Qdrant Edge, an embedded in-process engine with no background services, and a one-command Docker quickstart for a lightweight local instance. Community users independently confirm an in-memory mode "similar to sqlite" that makes POCs easy, and describe small portable binaries. missing for 10: in-depth first-party docs on Qdrant Edge setup and API beyond a summary line, first-party documentation of the client in-memory/local mode for development use.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the database embedded in-process or as a lightweight local instance for development and small workloads

citations.quote: Qdrant Edge is a lightweight, embedded vector search engine for in-process retrieval — no background services, minimal memory footprint, and no network required.
One of the big advantages of Qdrant is how easy it is to do a POC because it allows an 'in-memory' version similar to sqlite.
